chunks: And Ahmad ibn Abdun, known as Ibn al-Hashir, informed me, from Abul Hasan Muhammad ibn Ali al-Shajai al-Katib, from Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Nu'mani, from Yusuf ibn Ahmad (Muhammad) al-Ja'fari, who said:

I performed Hajj in the year 306 A.H., and stayed in Mecca that year and the following years until 309 A.H., then I left it returning to Syria. While I was on one of the roads, and the Morning Prayer had been missed by me, I descended from the litter and prepared for prayer. I saw four men in a litter, so I stopped, amazed at them. One of them said: 'At what are you amazed? You have missed your prayer and gone against your religion.' I said to the one who spoke to me: 'How do you know my religion?' He said: 'You wish to see the Master of your Time.' I said: 'Yes.' He indicated to one of the four. I said to him: 'He has signs and indications.' He said: 'Which is more pleasing to you: to see the camel and what is upon it ascending to the sky, or to see the litter ascending to the sky?' I said: 'Whatever of these occurs is a sign.' I saw the camel and what was upon it rising to the sky. The man had indicated to a man with a ruddy complexion, whose color was like gold, and between his eyes was a prayer mat.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الزَّمَانِ: Master of the Time (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What sign did the companion of the Imam of the Time offer to confirm his identity?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the concept of the Imam’s hidden presence during the Minor Occultation, where a companion identifies the Imam through a miraculous sign. The ascent of the camel and its load, rather than just the litter, serves as a divine confirmation of the Imam’s authority and distinctiveness, reinforcing the Shia belief in the tangible yet concealed nature of the Twelfth Imam.
